title: The Smoke Detector
evidence_boundary: False-alarm bias and anxiety loops described with 'may'; no diagnostic claims. Mirror-voice is a storytelling device, not therapy.
desired_movement: From obeying every internal alarm to checking reality with it - recalibration, not silence.
grounding: 3am bedroom, phone screen, door lock, kitchen table, morning curtains.
invitation: Which alarms in your house are set too sensitive - and who set them?
visual_doctrine_note: Message-mode determines slide type: desc=graphic+caption, abstract=psychedelic, story=people acting, metaphor=object still+effects.

scenes.text: Look at you. Three in the morning again, wide awake, chest tight, scanning for what's wrong. Can we talk about that alarm going off in you? Because I don't think it means what you think it means.
scenes.query: bathroom mirror at night, reflection leaning on sink, single bulb

scenes.text: Right now, somewhere in your body, there's a signal firing. You've been treating it like a prophecy. Like it knows something. That's the first thing we need to look at together.
scenes.image_prompt: cinematic still photograph, moody lighting, shallow depth of field, smoke detector on a dark ceiling, single red indicator light glowing

scenes.text: Your alarm system was installed a long time ago. And here's what nobody told you: it was never built to be accurate. It was built to be early.
scenes.query: old house hallway at night, warm lamp, long shadows

scenes.text: The part of you that fires that signal can't tell a real threat from a remembered one. It reacts to burnt toast and housefires with the same siren. A false alarm bias, wired in early. It may be why your line survived.
scenes.image_prompt: minimal flat design schematic, dark slate background, glowing amber linework, clean vector style, cinematic lighting, stylized brain profile with a small glowing alarm node, radiating concentric pulse rings

scenes.text: Watch yourself today. The email that made your stomach drop. The pause before you opened it. That wasn't danger. That was the siren doing what sirens do.
scenes.query: hand hesitating over glowing phone screen in dark room

scenes.text: And here's where it gets strange. The alarm doesn't just report your world. It colors it. Once it fires, everything looks like evidence. The feeling paints the room.
scenes.image_prompt: psychedelic flowing visual, alarm-red waves bleeding through a calm geometric fractal field, colors saturating everything they touch

scenes.text: So you check the locks again. Reread the text again. Rehearse the conversation again. Not because there's fire. Because checking is what the alarm asks for. And every check tells it the alarm was right.
scenes.query: door lock being tested at night, kitchen kettle steam, restless pacing shadow

scenes.text: That loop has a shape. Alarm. Check. Relief. And the relief trains the alarm to fire sooner next time. You haven't been calming it. You may have been training it.
scenes.image_prompt: minimal flat design schematic, dark slate background, glowing amber linework, clean vector style, cinematic lighting, circular loop diagram of four glowing nodes connected by arrows, one node flaring brighter

scenes.text: Now the real question. Who set your sensitivity? Because you didn't. Somebody taught your system what counts as smoke. A loud house. A quiet leaving. A year nobody explained.
scenes.image_prompt: cinematic still photograph, moody lighting, shallow depth of field, opened smoke detector showing a small sensitivity dial, a finger's shadow across it

scenes.text: Some of your alarms were calibrated by a childhood that needed them. Back then, reading a room fast mattered. Hearing footsteps mattered. Your sensitivity was intelligence. It kept a smaller you safe.
scenes.query: staircase at night from low angle, warm light under a door

scenes.text: But look around. You're not there anymore. The alarm is still guarding a house you moved out of years ago. It never got the memo. That's not damage. That's devotion with an old map.
scenes.query: calm sunlit apartment morning, curtains moving, coffee steam

scenes.text: So what do you do with an alarm you can't argue with? You stop arguing. You don't debate a siren. You check the kitchen.
scenes.image_prompt: psychedelic flowing visual, chaotic red spiral resolving into slow calm blue geometry, settling motion

scenes.text: Next time it fires, try this. Don't ask, what if it's right. Ask, what would I see if I actually looked? Then look. Slowly. Like someone checking a kitchen, not fleeing a fire.
scenes.query: slow breath by a window, hand flat on chest, morning light

scenes.text: The alarm says everything. The kitchen shows toast, most days. Keep the score if you have to. Ten alarms. How many fires? Your own data will out-argue your fear better than I ever could.
scenes.image_prompt: minimal flat design schematic, dark slate background, glowing amber linework, clean vector style, cinematic lighting, two-column tally board schematic, left column crowded with marks, right column nearly empty

scenes.text: And when it's toast, and it will mostly be toast, you don't punish the detector. You thank it. It's not broken. It's early. There's a difference, and the difference is the whole thing.
scenes.query: two friends laughing quietly at a kitchen table, easy body language

scenes.text: Some alarms you'll recalibrate. Some you'll just stop obeying. Both count. The goal was never silence. A house with no detector isn't peaceful. It's unprotected. You want a detector you can live with.
scenes.image_prompt: cinematic still photograph, moody lighting, shallow depth of field, smoke detector with a steady slow-blinking green light on a clean ceiling

scenes.text: There may be a day the siren fires and it's real. And here's what the practice buys you: a self that can tell the difference. That self moves faster than panic ever did.
scenes.image_prompt: psychedelic flowing visual, vast calm dark field with one small warm pulsing light, immense quiet space

scenes.text: So. Back to three in the morning. The tightness comes. And this time you say: I hear you. I'm checking. And you look, and the room is just a room, and the night is just a night.
scenes.query: bedroom at night, person sitting up calmly, soft dark blue light

scenes.text: You were never broken for having a loud alarm. You were unsupervised with it. That ends when you start doing the checking.
scenes.image_prompt: minimal flat design schematic, dark slate background, glowing amber linework, clean vector style, cinematic lighting, single centered glowing underline element on dark background, spotlight framing empty caption space

scenes.text: Which alarms in your house are set too sensitive? And who set them? Don't answer fast. Walk your rooms this week. Listen for which sirens are guarding fires that went out years ago.
scenes.query: person opening curtains to full daylight, rooms brightening

scenes.text: This is The Reality Machine. If this one found you at the right alarm, you know where we are. Come back anytime. We check kitchens here.
scenes.image_prompt: cinematic still photograph, moody lighting, shallow depth of field, smoke detector at dusk light, calm ceiling, warm window glow below
